# std.geometry

Plane and 3D geometry on exact integer points (`Pt`, `Pt3`) and careful floating-point vectors (`Vec`). Exact predicates compute cross and dot signs in `I128` so integer geometry is the default overflow-free path:  - `|x|, |y| <= 1e9` (e.g. `Pt<-1e9..=1e9>`): differences in `[-2e9, 2e9]`; single-vector `dot`/`cross` <= `2e18` fit `Int`, `turn`/`cross128`/`dot128` <= `8e18` fit `I128` with 19 orders of magnitude to spare, and `any_segments_meet` sweep comparisons <= `1.6e28` fit `I128`. - `|x|, |y| <= 2e18`: `turn`/`cross128`/`dot128`/`dist2_128` <= `8e36` fit `I128`. - 3D `|x|, |y|, |z| <= 1e9`: `cross3` components <= `8e18` fit `Int` (or `I128` up to `1e12`), and `convex_hull_3d` orientation tests <= `4.8e28` fit `I128`.

In prelude (no `use` needed): `ByAngle`, `Location`, `Pt`, `locate`, `turn`.

## Types & Constants

- `const PI: F64 = 3.14159265358979323846` — \(O(1)\).

## `struct Pt(pub x: Int, pub y: Int)`

\(O(1)\) value type.

- `@get fn norm2(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The squared length `x*x + y*y`, in `Int`.; traps: when the result overflows `Int`
- `@get fn norm2_128(self) -> I128` — \(O(1)\); The exact squared length `x*x + y*y`, computed in `I128`.; traps: when the result overflows `I128` (only for coordinates near `Int.MIN`)
- `@get fn len(self) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The Euclidean length `sqrt(x*x + y*y)` as `F64` (`hypot`, so no intermediate overflow).
- `@get fn perp(self) -> Pt` — \(O(1)\); `self` rotated 90 degrees counter-clockwise: `Pt(-y, x)`.; traps: when `y` is `Int.MIN`
- `@get fn perp_cw(self) -> Pt` — \(O(1)\); `self` rotated 90 degrees clockwise: `Pt(y, -x)`.; traps: when `x` is `Int.MIN`
- `@get fn angle(self) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The polar angle `atan2(y, x)` in `(-pi, pi]`; 0 for the zero vector.
- `fn unit_dir(self) -> Pt` — \(O(\log \max(\lvert x \rvert, \lvert y \rvert))\); The reduced integer direction `(x / g, y / g)` with `g = gcd(\|x\|, \|y\|)`; `Pt(0, 0)` for the zero vector.
- `@get fn to_vec(self) -> Vec` — \(O(1)\); `self` as a floating-point `Vec(F64(x), F64(y))`: the explicit way across.
- `fn dot(self, o: Pt) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The dot product `x * o.x + y * o.y`, in `Int`.; traps: when the result or a product overflows `Int`
- `fn dot128(self, o: Pt) -> I128` — \(O(1)\); The exact dot product `x * o.x + y * o.y`, computed in `I128`.; traps: when the sum overflows `I128` (only when every coordinate is near `Int.MIN`)
- `fn cross(self, o: Pt) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The 2D cross product `x * o.y - y * o.x`, in `Int`: positive when `o` is counter-clockwise from `self`, negative when clockwise, 0 when parallel.; traps: when the result or a product overflows `Int`
- `fn cross128(self, o: Pt) -> I128` — \(O(1)\); The exact 2D cross product `x * o.y - y * o.x`, computed in `I128`.; traps: when the difference overflows `I128` (only for coordinates near `Int.MIN`)
- `fn dist2(self, o: Pt) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The squared Euclidean distance from `self` to `o`, in `Int`.; traps: when the result overflows `Int`
- `fn dist2_128(self, o: Pt) -> I128` — \(O(1)\); The exact squared Euclidean distance from `self` to `o`, computed in `I128`.; traps: when the result overflows `I128` (coordinates beyond about `4e18` apart)
- `fn dist(self, o: Pt) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The Euclidean distance from `self` to `o`, as `F64`.
- `fn manhattan(self, o: Pt) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The Manhattan (L1) distance `\|x - o.x\| + \|y - o.y\|`.; traps: when the result overflows `Int`
- `fn chebyshev(self, o: Pt) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The Chebyshev (L-infinity) distance `max(\|x - o.x\|, \|y - o.y\|)`.; traps: when the result overflows `Int`

## `struct OnlineHull`

\(O(n)\) memory.

Fields: `hull: List<Pt>`.

- `fn new() -> OnlineHull` — \(O(1)\); An empty online convex hull.
- `fn add(mut self, p: Pt) -> Bool` — \(O(\log n)\) amortized; Insert `p` and report whether the hull changed (whether `p` is now a corner).
- `fn locate(self, p: Pt) -> Location` — \(O(\log n)\); Where `p` is relative to the current hull: `Inside`, `Boundary` or `Outside`.
- `fn extreme(self, dir: Pt) -> ?Pt` — \(O(\log n)\); The hull corner maximizing `v.dot128(dir)`, or `None` when the hull is empty.
- `@get fn area2(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); Twice the area of the current hull; 0 with fewer than 3 non-collinear points.; traps: when the value overflows `Int`
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of hull corners.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Whether no point has been added since creation or the last `clear`.
- `fn vertices(self) -> List<Pt>` — \(O(n)\) time and memory; The current hull corners, counter-clockwise from the least `(x, y)`.
- `fn iter(self) -> yields Pt` — \(O(n)\); The current hull corners, yielded in `vertices()` order without building a list.
- `fn clear(mut self)` — \(O(n)\); Remove every point; the hull is then empty.

## `struct Vec(pub x: F64, pub y: F64)`

\(O(1)\) value type.

- `@get fn norm2(self) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The squared length `x*x + y*y`.
- `@get fn len(self) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The Euclidean length (`hypot(x, y)`, so no intermediate overflow).
- `@get fn perp(self) -> Vec` — \(O(1)\); `self` rotated 90 degrees counter-clockwise: `Vec(-y, x)`.
- `@get fn perp_cw(self) -> Vec` — \(O(1)\); `self` rotated 90 degrees clockwise: `Vec(y, -x)`.
- `@get fn angle(self) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The polar angle `atan2(y, x)` in `(-pi, pi]`; a `-0.0` `y` counts as `0.0`, so the negative x axis gives `PI`, and the zero vector gives 0.0.
- `fn from_angle(rad: F64) -> Vec` — \(O(1)\); The unit vector `Vec(cos(rad), sin(rad))`.
- `@get fn unit(self) -> Vec` — \(O(1)\); The unit vector in the direction of `self`: each coordinate divided by `self.len`.; traps: when `self.len == 0.0`
- `fn rot(self, by: Vec) -> Vec` — \(O(1)\); `self` rotated by the direction `by`, as the complex product `self * by`: `Vec(x * by.x - y * by.y, x * by.y + y * by.x)`.
- `fn dot(self, o: Vec) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The dot product `x * o.x + y * o.y`.
- `fn cross(self, o: Vec) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The 2D cross product `x * o.y - y * o.x`: positive when `o` is counter-clockwise from `self`.
- `fn dist2(self, o: Vec) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The squared Euclidean distance from `self` to `o`.
- `fn dist(self, o: Vec) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The Euclidean distance from `self` to `o`.

## `struct Circle(pub c: Vec, pub r: F64)`

\(O(1)\) value type.

- `fn through(a: Vec, b: Vec, c: Vec, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> ?Circle` — \(O(1)\); The circle through `a`, `b` and `c`: centre `circumcenter(a, b, c, eps)`, radius its distance to `a`; `None` when collinear.
- `@get fn area(self) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The disk area, computed as `PI * r * r`.
- `@get fn circumference(self) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The circumference, computed as `2.0 * PI * r`.
- `fn locate(self, p: Vec, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> Location` — \(O(1)\); Where `p` is relative to the disk, with `d = c.dist(p)`: `Boundary` when `\|d - r\| <= eps`, else `Inside` when `d < r`, else `Outside`.

## `struct HalfPlane(p: Vec, dir: Vec)`

\(O(1)\) value type.

- `fn through(a: Vec, b: Vec) -> HalfPlane` — \(O(1)\); The closed half-plane left of the directed line `a -> b`: `HalfPlane(a, b - a)`.; traps: when `a == b`
- `fn from_line(a: F64, b: F64, c: F64) -> HalfPlane` — \(O(1)\); The half-plane `{ (x, y) \| a*x + b*y + c >= 0 }`, as `HalfPlane(p, Vec(b, -a))` with `p` the line's point nearest the origin, `Vec(-a * c, -b * c) / (a*a + b*b)`.; traps: when `a == 0.0` and `b == 0.0`
- `fn side(self, q: Vec) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The signed value `dir.cross(q - p)`: positive left of the line (inside), 0 on it, negative outside.

## `struct Rect(pub x: Range<Int>, pub y: Range<Int>)`

\(O(1)\) value type.

- `@get fn area(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of unit cells, `x.len * y.len`; 0 when either range is empty.; traps: when the product overflows `Int`
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Whether either axis range is empty.
- `fn contains(self, p: Pt) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Whether `p.x` is in `x` and `p.y` is in `y` (half-open, so the top and right edges are out).
- `fn intersect(self, o: Rect) -> ?Rect` — \(O(1)\); The common part of two rectangles, or `None` when it is empty (including rectangles that only touch along an edge).

## `struct Pt3(pub x: Int, pub y: Int, pub z: Int)`

\(O(1)\) value type.

- `@get fn norm2(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The squared length `x*x + y*y + z*z`, in `Int`.; traps: when the result overflows `Int`
- `@get fn norm2_128(self) -> I128` — \(O(1)\); The exact squared length, computed in `I128`.; traps: when the result overflows `I128`
- `@get fn len(self) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The Euclidean length as `F64`.
- `@get fn to_vec3(self) -> Vec3` — \(O(1)\); `self` as a floating-point `Vec3`: the explicit way across.
- `fn dot(self, o: Pt3) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The dot product `x * o.x + y * o.y + z * o.z`, in `Int`.; traps: when the result or a product overflows `Int`
- `fn dot128(self, o: Pt3) -> I128` — \(O(1)\); The exact dot product, computed in `I128`.; traps: when the sum overflows `I128`
- `fn cross(self, o: Pt3) -> Pt3` — \(O(1)\); The cross product `Pt3(y*o.z - z*o.y, z*o.x - x*o.z, x*o.y - y*o.x)`, perpendicular to both by the right-hand rule.; traps: when a component overflows `Int`
- `fn dist2(self, o: Pt3) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The squared Euclidean distance from `self` to `o`, in `Int`.; traps: when the result overflows `Int`
- `fn dist(self, o: Pt3) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The Euclidean distance from `self` to `o`, as `F64`.
- `fn manhattan(self, o: Pt3) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The Manhattan (L1) distance `\|x - o.x\| + \|y - o.y\| + \|z - o.z\|`.; traps: when the result overflows `Int`
- `fn chebyshev(self, o: Pt3) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The Chebyshev (L-infinity) distance `max(\|x - o.x\|, \|y - o.y\|, \|z - o.z\|)`.; traps: when the result overflows `Int`

## `struct Vec3(pub x: F64, pub y: F64, pub z: F64)`

\(O(1)\) value type.

- `@get fn norm2(self) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The squared length `x*x + y*y + z*z`.
- `@get fn len(self) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The Euclidean length.
- `@get fn unit(self) -> Vec3` — \(O(1)\); The unit vector in the direction of `self`: each coordinate divided by `self.len`.; traps: when `self.len == 0.0`
- `fn dot(self, o: Vec3) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The dot product `x * o.x + y * o.y + z * o.z`.
- `fn cross(self, o: Vec3) -> Vec3` — \(O(1)\); The cross product, by the right-hand rule, as for `Pt3.cross`.
- `fn dist2(self, o: Vec3) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The squared Euclidean distance from `self` to `o`.
- `fn dist(self, o: Vec3) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The Euclidean distance from `self` to `o`.
- `fn rot(self, axis: Vec3, rad: F64) -> Vec3` — \(O(1)\); `self` rotated by `rad` radians counter-clockwise about the unit vector `axis` (seen with `axis` pointing at the viewer), by Rodrigues' formula `v cos t + axis.cross(v) sin t + axis * axis.dot(v) * (1 - cos t)`.

## `struct Plane3(pub n: Vec3, pub d: F64)`

\(O(1)\) value type.

- `fn through(a: Vec3, b: Vec3, c: Vec3, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> ?Plane3` — \(O(1)\); The plane through `a`, `b` and `c`: `n = (b - a).cross(c - a).unit`, `d = n.dot(a)`; `None` when `(b - a).cross(c - a).len <= eps` (collinear).
- `fn dist(self, p: Vec3) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The signed distance `n.dot(p) - d`: positive on the side `n` points to.
- `fn project(self, p: Vec3) -> Vec3` — \(O(1)\); The orthogonal projection of `p` onto the plane: `p - n * self.dist(p)`.

## Functions

- `fn turn(a: Pt, b: Pt, c: Pt) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); Which way the path `a -> b -> c` turns: 1 left (counter-clockwise), -1 right, 0 straight.
- `fn same_dir(a: Pt, b: Pt) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Whether `a` and `b` are both nonzero and point the same way: parallel with a positive dot product, exact in `I128`.
- `fn angle_less(a: Pt, b: Pt, from: Pt = Pt(1, 0)) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Whether `a` comes before `b` counter-clockwise, starting from the ray `from` (default `+x`).; traps: when `from` is the zero vector
- `fn arg(p: Pt) -> ByAngle` — \(O(1)\); An exact, float-free angular sort key for `p`: `ByAngle(p)`, ordered as `angle_less` from `+x`.
- `fn on_segment(p: Pt, a: Pt, b: Pt, strict: Bool = false) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Whether `p` lies on the closed segment from `a` to `b`, exact in `I128`.
- `fn segments_meet(a: Pt, b: Pt, c: Pt, d: Pt, strict: Bool = false) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Whether the closed segments `a b` and `c d` share a point, exact in `I128`.
- `fn lower_hull(sorted_pts: List<Pt>, collinear: Bool = false) -> List<Pt>` — \(O(n)\) time and memory; The lower convex hull chain, left to right, of points sorted by `(x, y)` (Andrew's monotone chain).; traps: when `sorted_pts` is not sorted by `(x, y)`
- `fn upper_hull(sorted_pts: List<Pt>, collinear: Bool = false) -> List<Pt>` — \(O(n)\) time and memory; The upper convex hull chain, left to right, of points sorted by `(x, y)`; the mirror of `lower_hull`, with the same rules for duplicates and `collinear`.; traps: when `sorted_pts` is not sorted by `(x, y)`
- `fn convex_hull(pts: List<Pt>, collinear: Bool = false) -> List<Pt>` — \(O(n \log n)\) time, \(O(n)\) memory; The convex hull of `pts`, counter-clockwise from the least `(x, y)` point.
- `fn convex_hull_idx<D>(pts: [D]Pt, collinear: Bool = false) -> List<D>` — \(O(n \log n)\) time, \(O(n)\) memory; The convex hull of `pts` as domain positions `D` instead of copied points; otherwise as `convex_hull`.
- `fn lower_hull_idx<D>(pts: [D]Pt, collinear: Bool = false) -> List<D>` — \(O(n)\) time and memory; The lower hull chain of `(x, y)`-sorted `pts` as domain positions, left to right; otherwise as `lower_hull`, and equal points keep the smallest position.; traps: when `pts` is not sorted by `(x, y)` in key order
- `fn upper_hull_idx<D>(pts: [D]Pt, collinear: Bool = false) -> List<D>` — \(O(n)\) time and memory; The upper hull chain of `(x, y)`-sorted `pts` as domain positions, left to right; otherwise as `upper_hull`, and equal points keep the smallest position.; traps: when `pts` is not sorted by `(x, y)` in key order
- `fn minkowski_sum(a: List<Pt>, b: List<Pt>) -> List<Pt>` — \(O(\lvert a \rvert + \lvert b \rvert)\) time and memory; The Minkowski sum `{p + q}` of two non-empty counter-clockwise convex polygons, by merging edges.; traps: when `a` or `b` is empty
- `fn minkowski_upper(a: List<Pt>, b: List<Pt>) -> List<Pt>` — \(O(\lvert a \rvert + \lvert b \rvert)\) time and memory; The upper hull of the Minkowski sum of two non-empty left-to-right upper hulls.; traps: when `a` or `b` is empty
- `fn minkowski_lower(a: List<Pt>, b: List<Pt>) -> List<Pt>` — \(O(\lvert a \rvert + \lvert b \rvert)\) time and memory; The lower hull of the Minkowski sum of two non-empty left-to-right lower hulls; the mirror of `minkowski_upper`.; traps: when `a` or `b` is empty
- `fn convex_polygons_overlap(a: List<Pt>, b: List<Pt>) -> Bool` — \(O(\lvert a \rvert + \lvert b \rvert)\); Whether two non-empty counter-clockwise convex polygons share at least one point, boundary included.; traps: when `a` or `b` is empty
- `fn convex_polygon_intersect(a: List<Vec>, b: List<Vec>, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> List<Vec>` — \(O(\lvert a \rvert + \lvert b \rvert)\) time and memory; The intersection of two counter-clockwise convex polygons, as a counter-clockwise polygon.
- `fn area2(poly: List<Pt>) -> Int` — \(O(n)\); Twice the signed area of the polygon `poly` (shoelace): positive when the vertices run counter-clockwise, negative when clockwise; 0 for fewer than 3 vertices.; traps: when the sum overflows `Int`
- `fn area2_128(poly: List<Pt>) -> I128` — \(O(n)\); Twice the signed area of `poly`, as `area2`, accumulated exactly in `I128`.; traps: when the sum overflows `I128`
- `fn locate(poly: List<Pt>, p: Pt) -> Location` — \(O(n)\); Where `p` is relative to the simple polygon `poly`, in either orientation: `Inside`, `Boundary` or `Outside`.
- `fn locate_convex(hull: List<Pt>, p: Pt) -> Location` — \(O(\log n)\); Where `p` is relative to the counter-clockwise convex polygon `hull`: `Inside`, `Boundary` or `Outside`, by binary search on the fan from `hull[0]`.
- `fn diameter2(hull: List<Pt>) -> Int` — \(O(n)\); The squared diameter of the counter-clockwise convex polygon `hull`: the largest `dist2` between two vertices, by rotating calipers.; traps: when the result overflows `Int`
- `fn min_bounding_box(hull: List<Pt>) -> (area: F64, perimeter: F64)` — \(O(n)\); The least area and the least perimeter of a rectangle enclosing the counter-clockwise convex polygon `hull`, each minimized on its own (by rotating calipers, exact in `I128` until the final division).
- `fn hull_extreme(hull: List<Pt>, dir: Pt) -> Int` — \(O(\log n)\); The index of a vertex of the non-empty counter-clockwise convex polygon `hull` maximizing `hull[i].dot128(dir)`, by binary search.; traps: when `hull` is empty
- `fn hull_tangents(hull: List<Pt>, p: Pt) -> (left: Int, right: Int)` — \(O(\log n)\); The indices `(left, right)` of the tangent vertices from a strictly exterior point `p` to a strictly convex counter-clockwise polygon `hull` (`hull.len >= 3`).; traps: when `hull.len < 3` or `p` is not strictly outside
- `fn closest_pair2(pts: List<Pt>) -> Int` — \(O(n \log n)\) time, \(O(n)\) memory; The least squared distance between two points of `pts` at distinct positions (0 when two are equal), by divide and conquer.; traps: when `pts.len < 2`, or a distance overflows `Int`
- `fn closest_pair<D>(pts: [D]Pt) -> (a: D, b: D, dist2: Int)` — \(O(n \log n)\) time, \(O(n)\) memory; The closest pair of distinct positions `a` before `b` in key order, with their squared distance.; traps: when `pts` has fewer than 2 points, or a distance overflows `Int`
- `fn hull_width(hull: List<Pt>) -> F64` — \(O(n)\); The least width of the counter-clockwise convex polygon `hull`: the smallest distance between two parallel supporting lines, by rotating calipers.
- `fn hull_line_intersect(hull: List<Pt>, a: Pt, b: Pt) -> ?(Int, Int)` — \(O(\log n)\); The two edges of the counter-clockwise convex polygon `hull` that the line through `a` and `b` crosses, as `(i, j)` with `i < j`, or `None` if the line misses the interior.; traps: when `a == b`
- `fn farthest_pair<D>(pts: [D]Pt) -> (a: D, b: D, dist2: Int)` — \(O(n \log n)\) time, \(O(n)\) memory; The farthest pair of distinct positions `a` before `b` in key order, with their squared distance (convex hull, then rotating calipers).; traps: when `pts` has fewer than 2 points, or a distance overflows `Int`
- `fn manhattan_mst<D>(pts: [D]Pt) -> List<(u: D, v: D, w: Int)>` — \(O(n \log n)\) time, \(O(n)\) memory; At most `4n` candidate edges `(u, v, w)` that contain a minimum spanning tree of `pts` under the Manhattan distance `w = pts[u].manhattan(pts[v])`.; traps: when a distance overflows `Int`
- `fn polygon_centroid(poly: List<Vec>) -> Vec` — \(O(n)\); The centroid (centre of mass) of the region inside the simple polygon `poly`, either orientation.; traps: when the polygon has zero area
- `fn polygon_kernel(poly: List<Vec>, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> List<Vec>` — \(O(n \log n)\) time, \(O(n)\) memory; The kernel of the counter-clockwise simple polygon `poly`: the points that see the whole interior, as a counter-clockwise convex polygon (half-plane intersection of the edges).
- `fn polygon_triangulate(poly: List<Pt>) -> List<(Int, Int, Int)>` — \(O(n \log n)\) time, \(O(n)\) memory; A triangulation of the counter-clockwise simple polygon `poly` into `n - 2` triangles of vertex indices, each listed counter-clockwise.; traps: when `poly` is not counter-clockwise
- `fn pick_interior(poly: List<Pt>) -> Int` — \(O(n \log \mathit{max\_coord})\); The number of lattice points strictly inside the simple lattice polygon `poly`, either orientation, by Pick's theorem: `I = (\|area2\| - B) / 2 + 1` with `B = pick_boundary(poly)`.; traps: when `poly` has fewer than 3 vertices, or the area overflows `Int`
- `fn pick_boundary(poly: List<Pt>) -> Int` — \(O(n \log \mathit{max\_coord})\); The number of lattice points on the boundary of the lattice polygon `poly`: the sum of `gcd(\|dx\|, \|dy\|)` over its edges, including the closing edge.; traps: when the sum overflows `Int`
- `fn close(a: F64, b: F64, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Whether `\|a - b\| <= eps`: an absolute tolerance, the same test every `eps` in this module uses.
- `fn sign_eps(x: F64, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The sign of `x` with tolerance: 1 if `x > eps`, -1 if `x < -eps`, else 0.
- `fn turn_eps(a: Vec, b: Vec, c: Vec, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); Which way the path `a -> b -> c` turns, with tolerance: `sign_eps((b - a).cross(c - a), eps)`, so 1 left, -1 right, 0 straight within `eps`.
- `fn angle_between(a: Vec, b: Vec) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The signed angle from `a` to `b`, `atan2(a.cross(b), a.dot(b))`, in `(-pi, pi]`: positive when `b` is counter-clockwise from `a`.
- `fn project(p: Vec, a: Vec, b: Vec) -> Vec` — \(O(1)\); The orthogonal projection of `p` onto the line through `a` and `b`: `a + (b - a) * ((p - a).dot(b - a) / (b - a).norm2)`.; traps: when `a == b`
- `fn reflect(p: Vec, a: Vec, b: Vec) -> Vec` — \(O(1)\); The mirror image of `p` across the line through `a` and `b`: `project(p, a, b) * 2.0 - p`.; traps: when `a == b`
- `fn line_dist(p: Vec, a: Vec, b: Vec) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The perpendicular distance from `p` to the infinite line through `a` and `b`: `\|(b - a).cross(p - a)\| / (b - a).len`.; traps: when `a == b`
- `fn seg_dist(p: Vec, a: Vec, b: Vec, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The shortest distance from `p` to the closed segment `a b`: to the projection when it falls inside the segment, else to the nearer endpoint.
- `fn line_intersect(a: Vec, b: Vec, c: Vec, d: Vec, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> ?Vec` — \(O(1)\); The intersection of the infinite lines `a b` and `c d`, or `None` when `\|(b - a).cross(d - c)\| <= eps` (parallel or coincident).
- `fn segment_intersect(a: Vec, b: Vec, c: Vec, d: Vec, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> List<Vec>` — \(O(1)\); The common points of the closed segments `a b` and `c d`: `[]` when disjoint, one point when they cross or touch, and the two ends of the shared piece when they overlap collinearly.
- `fn ray_hits_segment(o: Vec, dir: Vec, a: Vec, b: Vec, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> ?Vec` — \(O(1)\); The first point where the ray from `o` in direction `dir` meets the closed segment `a b`, or `None`.; traps: when `dir` is the zero vector
- `fn circumcenter(a: Vec, b: Vec, c: Vec, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> ?Vec` — \(O(1)\); The centre of the circle through `a`, `b` and `c`, or `None` when `\|(b - a).cross(c - a)\| <= eps` (collinear).
- `fn incenter(a: Vec, b: Vec, c: Vec, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> ?Circle` — \(O(1)\); The inscribed circle of the triangle `a b c`, or `None` when `\|(b - a).cross(c - a)\| <= eps` (collinear).
- `fn circle_line_intersect(circle: Circle, a: Vec, b: Vec, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> List<Vec>` — \(O(1)\); The points where `circle` meets the infinite line through `a` and `b`: two when it crosses, one (the foot of the perpendicular from the centre) when the distance is within `eps` of `r`, and None otherwise.; traps: when `a == b`
- `fn circle_intersect(a: Circle, b: Circle, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> List<Vec>` — \(O(1)\); The points where the circles `a` and `b` meet: two when they cross, one when tangent (within `eps`), None when apart, nested, or identical (infinitely many).
- `fn circle_tangents(circle: Circle, p: Vec, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> List<Vec>` — \(O(1)\); The points of `circle` where a tangent line through `p` touches it: two when `p` is outside, `[p]` when `p` is on the circle (within `eps`), None when inside.
- `fn circle_circle_tangents(a: Circle, b: Circle, inner: Bool = false, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> List<(Vec, Vec)>` — \(O(1)\); The common tangent segments `(p1, p2)` of the circles `a` and `b`, `p1` on `a` and `p2` on `b`: the outer tangents, or the inner ones (crossing between the centres) with `inner: true`.
- `fn circle_circle_area(a: Circle, b: Circle, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The area of the intersection of the disks `a` and `b`: 0.0 when apart, the smaller disk's `area` when one contains the other (within `eps`), else the sum of the two circular segments.
- `fn invert(p: Vec, across: Circle) -> Vec` — \(O(1)\); The inverse of `p` in the circle `across`: `c + (p - c) * (r * r / (p - c).norm2)`.; traps: when `p == across.c`
- `fn circles_union_area(circles: List<Circle>, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> F64` — \(O(n^2 \log n)\) time, \(O(n)\) memory; The area of the union of the disks `circles`, by Green's theorem over the arcs on the union's boundary.
- `fn half_plane_intersect(planes: List<HalfPlane>, bound: ?F64 = None, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> List<Vec>` — \(O(n \log n)\) time, \(O(n)\) memory; The intersection of the closed half-planes `planes`, as a counter-clockwise convex polygon (sort by angle, then a deque sweep).; traps: when a plane's `dir` is the zero vector
- `fn polygon_area(poly: List<Vec>) -> F64` — \(O(n)\); The signed area of the polygon `poly` (half the shoelace sum): positive counter-clockwise, negative clockwise; 0.0 for fewer than 3 vertices.
- `fn polygon_cut(poly: List<Vec>, a: Vec, b: Vec, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> List<Vec>` — \(O(n)\) time and memory; The part of `poly` in the closed half-plane left of the directed line `a -> b` (Sutherland-Hodgman).; traps: when `a == b`
- `fn min_enclosing_circle(pts: List<Vec>, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> Circle` — \(O(n)\) expected for unadversarial order; The smallest circle containing every point of `pts` (Welzl's algorithm, deterministic: points are processed in input order, with no shuffle).
- `fn circle_polygon_area(circle: Circle, poly: List<Vec>, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> F64` — \(O(n)\); The signed area of the intersection of the disk `circle` with the simple polygon `poly`: positive when `poly` is counter-clockwise, negative when clockwise.
- `fn any_segments_meet(segs: List<(a: Pt, b: Pt)>, strict: Bool = false) -> ?(Int, Int)` — \(O(n \log n)\) time, \(O(n)\) memory; Whether any two segments of `segs` share a point, by a Shamos-Hoey sweep with exact `I128` comparisons (valid for `\|x\|, \|y\| <= 1e12`): `Some((i, j))` with `i < j` for a pair that meets, or `None`.
- `fn any_segments_meet_idx<D>(segs: [D](a: Pt, b: Pt), strict: Bool = false) -> ?(D, D)` — \(O(n \log n)\) time, \(O(n)\) memory; `any_segments_meet` over a domain-indexed array: `Some((a, b))` with `a` before `b` in key order for a pair of segments that meet, or `None`.
- `fn rects_union_area(rects: List<Rect>) -> Int` — \(O(n \log n)\) time, \(O(n)\) memory; The area of the union of `rects`, by a sweep over x with a segment tree over the compressed y coordinates.; traps: when the area overflows `Int`
- `fn planar_faces<V>(pts: [V]Pt, edges: List<(V, V)>) -> List<List<V>>` — \(O((n + m) \log m)\) time, \(O(n + m)\) memory; The faces of the planar straight-line graph with vertices `pts` and undirected `edges`, each as its cycle of vertices: bounded faces counter-clockwise, the outer face of each connected component clockwise.; traps: when an edge joins a vertex to itself, or an edge repeats
- `fn point_location_planar<V>(pts: [V]Pt, edges: List<(V, V)>, queries: List<Pt>) -> List<?Int>` — \(O((n + m + q) \log(n + m))\) time, \(O(n + m + q)\) memory; For each query point, the index into `planar_faces(pts, edges)` of the bounded face that contains it, or `None` when it lies on an edge or vertex or in the unbounded region (offline sweep).; traps: as `planar_faces`
- `fn delaunay<D>(pts: [D]Pt) -> List<(D, D, D)>` — \(O(n \log n)\) time, \(O(n)\) memory; The Delaunay triangulation of distinct integer points (`\|coords\| <= 1e9`), exact in `I128`, as counter-clockwise handle triples.; traps: when two points are equal
- `fn voronoi_cells<D>(pts: [D]Pt, bound: F64) -> [D]List<Vec>` — \(O(n \log n)\) time, \(O(n)\) memory; The Voronoi cell of each point, clipped to the box `[-bound, bound]^2`, as a counter-clockwise polygon (from the Delaunay dual, then half-plane clipping).; traps: when two points are equal or `bound <= 0.0`
- `fn convex_hull_3d(pts: List<Pt3>) -> List<(Int, Int, Int)>` — \(O(n^2)\) time, \(O(n)\) memory; The 3D convex hull of `pts` as triangular faces of indices, each counter-clockwise seen from outside (so its normal points out), exact in `I128` (valid for `\|x\|, \|y\|, \|z\| <= 1e12`).
- `fn convex_hull_3d_idx<D>(pts: [D]Pt3) -> List<(D, D, D)>` — \(O(n^2)\) time, \(O(n)\) memory; `convex_hull_3d` over a domain-indexed array, with faces of handles; the same orientation, order and tie rules, in key order.
- `fn polyhedron_volume6(pts: List<Pt3>, faces: List<(Int, Int, Int)>) -> I128` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{faces} \rvert)\); Six times the signed volume of the closed triangulated surface `faces` over `pts`: the sum of `pts[a].dot128(pts[b].cross(pts[c]))` over faces, computed in `I128`.; traps: when a face index is out of range
- `fn line_plane_intersect(a: Vec3, b: Vec3, plane: Plane3, eps: F64 = 1e-9) -> ?Vec3` — \(O(1)\); The point where the infinite line through `a` and `b` meets `plane`, or `None` when `\|plane.n.dot(b - a)\| <= eps` (parallel, including lying in the plane, or `a == b`).
- `fn sphere_dist(a: Vec3, b: Vec3, r: F64 = 1.0) -> F64` — \(O(1)\); The great-circle distance between the directions of `a` and `b` on a sphere of radius `r`: `r * atan2(a.cross(b).len, a.dot(b))`.
- `fn dot(a: Pt, b: Pt) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The dot product `a.x * b.x + a.y * b.y`, the free form of `a.dot(b)`.; traps: overflow when a product leaves `Int`; use `dot128` style `I128` maths for coordinates past about 3e9
- `fn cross(a: Pt, b: Pt) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The cross product `a.x * b.y - a.y * b.x`, the free form of `a.cross(b)`: positive when `b` is counter-clockwise from `a`.; traps: overflow when a product leaves `Int`

## Example

```cp
let a = Pt(0, 0)
let b = Pt(3, 4)
print(a.dist2(b))
// output: 25
```
